note: Validation set for placement, fixed before any v4 run (October 21, 2026). Known-filled pairings come from established literatures with published reviews. Known-empty pairings are ones a 2022-2025 management article claims to be the first to study (OpenAlex ID of that article given). Idea texts are one-line paraphrases written for this test.

cases.idea: Does a strong CSR record license later misconduct? Firms that do good may feel entitled to cut corners later.
Do board interlocks confer organizational legitimacy? Firms tied through shared directors to well-regarded firms may borrow their legitimacy.
Does misconduct spread through an organization the way fatigue cracks grow in metal under repeated stress, with small violations accumulating until a sudden failure?
Do new ventures signal their quality to investors through costly signals such as founders' credentials, and does signaling help them raise funding?
cases.basis: signaling theory and venture finance (Connelly et al. 2011 review)

cases.idea: Does agency theory explain how boards design executive compensation, tying pay to performance to align CEOs' interests with shareholders'?
cases.basis: agency theory and executive pay (Devers et al. 2007 review)

cases.idea: Do employees reciprocate fair treatment through social exchange by engaging in organizational citizenship behavior?
cases.basis: social exchange and OCB (Podsakoff et al. 2000 review)

cases.idea: Do organizations adopt the same management practices as their peers through institutional isomorphism, imitating others to appear legitimate?
cases.basis: isomorphism and practice adoption (DiMaggio and Powell 1983 onward)

cases.idea: Does prospect theory explain managerial risk taking, with managers taking more risk when firm performance falls below their reference point?
cases.basis: prospect theory and managerial risk taking (Wiseman and Gomez-Mejia 1998 onward)

cases.idea: Do managers keep investing in failing projects because of escalation of commitment to their earlier decisions?
cases.basis: escalation of commitment (Sleesman et al. 2012 meta-analytic review)

cases.idea: During organizational crises, does collective sensemaking break down and shape how the crisis unfolds?
cases.basis: sensemaking in crises (Maitlis and Sonenshein 2010 review)

cases.idea: Does psychological contract breach lead employees to quit their organizations?
cases.basis: psychological contract breach and turnover (Zhao et al. 2007 meta-analysis)

cases.idea: Do top management team characteristics, as upper echelons theory proposes, explain firms' strategic change?
cases.basis: upper echelons and strategic change (Hambrick and Mason 1984 onward)

cases.idea: Does transaction cost economics explain firms' make-or-buy decisions, with asset specificity pushing them to integrate vertically?
cases.basis: transaction cost economics and vertical integration (David and Han 2004 review)

cases.idea: Does the fraud triangle of pressure, opportunity, and rationalization explain why firms hold ISO 14001 environmental certification without implementing it?
When an organization's leader commits a public transgression, does the transgression threaten members' identity, so that they disengage from the organization and stop buying from it?
Does the theory of planned behavior explain a firm's green innovation, with subjective norms coming from its supply chain partners?
Does a leader's humor spur employees' creative work behavior by raising their prosocial motivation?
In hostile takeovers, do the target's managers shape how employees respond through sensemaking and sensegiving?
Does the IKEA effect, valuing what one helped build, lead buyers to value supply chain relationships they built with their suppliers more highly?
Do recruiters' emotional reactions to risk, as the risk-as-feelings account proposes, shape their hiring decisions?
Does regime theory explain how the governance of ESG reporting forms, including who sets the rules for ESG disclosure?
Do firms adopt green supply chain practices in a sequence that builds cumulative capabilities, as the sand cone model proposes?
Does CEO narcissism drive firms' corporate political activity?
Does a corporate Stockholm syndrome explain why employees stay committed to consistently dysfunctional organizations?
Does temporal motivation theory explain why broad-based employee ownership affects productivity differently in family and nonfamily firms?
